pillars: Deep work consistency for side builders
Open source AI and cost-saving tool switches

plays.title: Share Your Daily Deep Work Routine Story
plays.description: Post personal, specific stories of doing 2 hours of focused side work every day while holding a full-time job. This resonates because it proves consistency over intensity and gives followers an exact template they can start tomorrow.
plays.action:
1. Choose a real multi-month streak of daily deep work on your own project.
2. Open with the hook: "I changed my life by just doing 2 hrs of deep work EVERY DAY for a year."
3. Paint the picture in 3 sentences: wake-up time, coffee shop grind for tiny progress on business, then full-time job.
4. Keep the whole post short and authentic.
5. Add a photo of your setup or a simple visual.
6. Engage replies by asking what their daily block looks like.

plays.title: Publish the AI Micro-Micro SaaS Weekend Blueprint
plays.description: Create a highly actionable checklist post teaching how to pick one feature from a $1B company and build a tiny version using AI tools (Claude/Grok + Cursor etc). This is proven to drive high engagement, bookmarks, and replies from builders ready to ship.
plays.action:
1. Identify one tiny single-feature idea inspired by a large successful company.
2. Start the tweet: "i've got your last 6 months of the year plans right here:"
3. List the steps using > blockquotes for visual scannability:
> block off 4 hours of your weekend
> pick a $1b company
> build a micro-micro version of it
> like one-single feature
> open claude/chatgpt/grok + cursor/windsurf, etc.
> type "i'm a noob. i wanna build something like this. guide me 1 step at time"
> copy/paste into cursor
> follow steps until it works
4. Close strongly: "voilà, you just built your first micro-saas"
5. Reply to your own post (or quote tweet) with a link to a database of real examples or projects.
6. Post late in the week so people can execute over the weekend.

plays.title: Share a Specific Open Source AI Tool Migration
plays.description: Tell the true story of cancelling a paid subscription and switching to a free, local, open source alternative that is better. Positions you as practical and bullish on the future of accessible tools while delivering high relatability and saves.
plays.action:
1. Select one paid tool (ideally $10-20/mo) you actually replaced with open source/local AI.
2. Lead the post with: "I'm bullish on open source AI."
3. Briefly state the old cost and tool name.
4. Explain the switch: download model, runs locally, and results in "better, faster, more private, and it's free!"
5. End with the open question: "I wonder what other subscriptions I can get rid of?"
6. Include a screenshot of the new tool in use for credibility.
7. Monitor and reply to comments with more tool suggestions.

plays.title: Frame Big Tech News as 'We Are Still So Early'
plays.description: When major AI or startup news drops (big valuations, acquisitions, model launches), publish a tight roundup list followed by the grounding perspective that the real opportunity is still ahead. Occasionally layer in the 'ignore the haters' proof of impact message.
plays.action:
1. Collect 3-4 actual headline events from the last few weeks.
2. Format cleanly as:
> Lovable hit $500M in June.
> Cursor got acquired for $60B.
> ...
3. Follow with: "All of this happened THIS MONTH!! We are still so early."
4. Use a supporting image (collage or bold graphic).
5. As a companion or alternate post: "try caring less about what strangers think about you on the internet one time a reddit mob created an actual petition to ban me and it got hundreds of upvotes nobody remembers it. my products have impacted millions"
6. Publish when news is fresh for maximum relevance and discussion.

hooks: i've got your last 6 months of the year plans right here:
I'm bullish on open source AI.
I changed my life by just doing 2 hrs of deep work EVERY DAY for a year.
try caring less about what strangers think about you on the internet
angles: Anyone can build their first micro-SaaS this weekend by cloning one feature with AI step-by-step
Open source local AI tools are already superior to paid subscriptions on every metric that matters
Small daily deep work sessions (while employed) are the real path to changing your life
Explosive industry headlines mean the best building opportunities are still in front of us
Online noise and criticism is temporary; shipped products and real user impact are permanent
